To assess transistor performance with A-TiO2 gate oxide, we measured 100 p- and 100 n-type devices across the wafer, randomly sampled from five representative regions (Supplementary Fig. 11), where the majority of devices have consistent electrical characteristics across the wafer. Devices were qualified by excluding those with abnormal Vth shifts, Ion/Ioff outside 106–5 × 107, or failed electrical characteristics. Figure 2e shows representative transfer characteristics (Ids – Vgs) of 80 qualified long-channel 1L-MoS2 FETs integrated with a 5.8-nm-thick A-TiO2 dielectric (EOT ≈ 0.88 nm; W/L = 2 μm/3 μm). The average subthreshold swing across the array is 68 mV dec–1, with the best device achieving 61 mV dec–1. Similarly, 84 qualified bilayer WSe2 (2L-WSe2) FETs (W/L = 2 μm/2 μm) with A-TiO2 dielectric show excellent performance (Fig. 2f), delivering average and minimum subthreshold swing values of 79 mV dec–1 and 65 mV dec–1, respectively. The subthreshold swing values as a function of Ids for selected 1L-MoS2/A-TiO2 and 2L-WSe2/A-TiO2 devices are presented in Supplementary Fig. 13. Statistical distributions of Ion/Ioff, subthreshold swing and Vth for the working p- and n-type transistors are summarized in Supplementary Fig. 12, with most n- and p-FETs (>98%) exhibiting over seven orders of magnitude in Ion/Ioff ratios, low gate leakage and minimal variation in Vth. Supplementary Fig. 14a and 14b further present representative transfer characteristics of 1L-MoS2 and 2L-WSe2 FETs integrated with thicker A-TiO2 gate dielectrics (18.2 nm; EOT ≈ 1.5 nm). Supplementary Fig. 14c–f show the corresponding gate leakage currents for 1L-MoS2 and 2L-WSe2 FETs with 18.2-nm and 5.8 nm A-TiO2 gate dielectrics, supporting that strong electrostatic control is maintained without increased leakage even under aggressive EOT scaling. Extended Data Fig. 3a compares the subthreshold swing versus EOT across various technologies using CVD-grown 2D channels. Extended Data Fig. 3b further compares Jleak at an applied gate voltage of 1 V for various gate-stack technologies with EOT or CET ≤ 1 nm. The A-TiO2 gate stack demonstrates low Jleak with sub-1-nm EOT, remaining well below the low-power limit (1.5 × 10−2 A cm−2). Recent studies have highlighted the trade-off between leakage-current suppression and electrostatic scaling in vdW-integrated 2D transistor interfaces31, and readers are referred to these works for broader discussions on EOT benchmarking and scaling considerations.

We further fabricated short-channel bottom-gated 1L-MoS2 and 2L-WSe2 FETs with channel lengths of about 50 nm to evaluate gate controllability at scaled dimensions. Even at this reduced channel length, both 1L-MoS2/A-TiO2 and 2L-WSe2/A-TiO2 devices exhibit near-ideal subthreshold swing (around 72 mV dec–1) and a high Ion/Ioff ratio (>108) without an increase in off-state current (Fig. 2g,h). The short-channel devices also have high Ion at Vds = 0.6 V. For the 1L-MoS2/A-TiO2 configuration, Ion reaches 227 μA μm–1 at Vov = 0.6 V and 167 μA μm–1 at Vov = 0.4 V. Similarly, the 2L-WSe2/A-TiO2 device demonstrates Ion values of 136 μA μm–1 (Vov = –0.6 V) and 86 μA μm–1 (Vov = –0.4 V) at a drain bias of –0.6 V, where Vov = Vgs − Vth denotes the gate-overdrive voltage. The corresponding output characteristics are shown in Fig. 2i. These results can be attributed to the superior gate-to-channel electrostatic control enabled by the A-TiO2 high-κ gate stack (Extended Data Fig. 4). Figure 2j benchmarks the subthreshold swing versus channel length (Lch) for reported short-channel 2D FETs using different dielectric technologies, highlighting that the subthreshold swing values achieved with A-TiO2 gate dielectric are among the lowest reported for CVD-grown MoS2 and WSe2 devices with similar structures. Supplementary Table 1 benchmarks devices using amorphous or single-crystal gate dielectrics with CVD-grown 2D TMD channel materials. The proposed A-TiO2 integration achieves a sub-1-nm EOT, a subthreshold swing of below 65 mV dec–1 and a high Ion, metrics which align with the requirements for low-power, high-performance logic applications.

Hysteresis in the transistor transfer characteristics is a critical metric of operational stability. Here we systematically compare 2D transistors integrated with single-crystalline A-TiO2 to those using amorphous HfO2 and Al2O3 gate dielectrics deposited by the ALD approach (Methods). Extended Data Fig. 5 displays the Ids – Vgs characteristics for different types of dielectrics under forward and reverse gate-voltage sweeps. The hysteresis width (ΔVH) of 1L-MoS2/A-TiO2 FETs reaches an exceptionally small value of around 1.5 mV at the sweeping frequency (f) of 0.028 Hz (f = 1/tsw, where tsw represents the total forward and backward sweeping time). The cyclostationary behavior of the 1L-MoS2/A-TiO2 FET is further detailed in Supplementary Fig. 15. The minimal variation observed between the initial and 100th measurement cycles supports the robustness of the gate stack and ensures that our hysteresis characterization is reliable for future device benchmarking32. For a fair comparison, ΔVH is normalized by EOT33,34. Figure 3a summarizes the statistical distribution of normalized ΔVH extracted from devices employing different dielectrics (Supplementary Fig. 16), where A-TiO2 has the smallest hysteresis value among all the tested devices. Supplementary Fig. 17 further shows normalized ΔVH as a function of sweep frequency for a representative 1L-MoS2/A-TiO2 FET measured under different gate sweeping ranges. The resulting hysteresis remains minimal across all measurement conditions, in sharp contrast to MoS2 transistors with conventional SiO2, Al2O3 or HfO2 gate dielectrics, which display pronounced hysteresis, particularly at low sweeping frequencies, due to slow charge trapping in oxide defect states35. Figure 3b benchmarks the normalized ΔVH of 1L-MoS2/A-TiO2 FETs against literature values reported for a range of dielectric technologies. Notably, our unencapsulated devices achieve a normalized ΔVH of 0.5 mV nm–1, which not only outperforms those of unencapsulated 2D transistors but also demonstrates superior stability compared with channel-encapsulated devices. Furthermore, bias-temperature instability (BTI) measurements reinforce the stability of the 1L-MoS2/A-TiO2 interface (Methods), revealing small threshold voltage shift (ΔVth) under both positive (ΔVth = 40 mV) and negative (ΔVth = 50 mV) gate bias stress (Supplementary Fig. 18). These results indicate the scarcity of border traps within the single-crystalline gate dielectric and a clean dielectric/2D semiconductor interface, even when integrated using conventional wet transfer technologies. Although the BTI of these 2D FETs currently exceeds that of established silicon technology3, further optimization of the interface and dielectric quality remains a clear path toward industrial parity.

a, Normalized hysteresis widths ΔVH with average (μ) and standard deviation (σ) values extracted from the MoS2 FETs with different gate dielectrics and thicknesses. b, Comparison of normalized ΔVH across high-κ dielectric technologies in 2D FETs18,19,22,49,50,51,52,53. Open and solid symbols denote amorphous and crystalline gate dielectrics, respectively. All benchmark values were extracted for 2 V < ΔVgs < 3.5 V and tsw ≤ 100 s. c, Typical cross-sectional STM topography image of the Au/TiO2 interface. Scale bar, 10 nm. d, Atomic-scale evolution of electronic properties of the subsurface of A-TiO2 and HfO2. e, Arrhenius plot of I-DLTS results extracted from 1L-MoS2/A-TiO2 and 1L-MoS2/HfO2 devices, revealing two distinct trap states. The table in the inset lists the activation energy (Ec – Et) and the capture cross section (σn) of two trap states, obtained from the slope and intercept of the two Arrhenius curves. f, Transfer characteristics of 2L-WSe2/A-TiO2 (green) and 2L-WSe2/HfO2 (purple) p-FETs. Both devices share identical channel dimensions (Lch = 2 μm, Wch = 2 μm), highlighting the impact of dielectric choice on FET devices.

The record-low hysteresis can be attributed to the clean channel–dielectric interface and crystalline dielectric with low concentration of traps, which together drastically suppress charge trapping to enable low hysteresis. The estimated interface trap density (Dit) is determined as approximately 5.74 × 1011 cm−2 eV−1, substantially lower than the values typically reported for devices incorporating CVD-grown MoS2 channels (Supplementary Table 2), although CVD-synthesized MoS2 inevitably contains point defects (1011–1012 cm–2) due to thermodynamic and growth chemistry constraints36. To understand the origin of hysteresis, we perform cross-sectional scanning tunneling microscope/spectroscopy (XSTM/S) measurements to directly probe the in-gap states in dielectric oxides (Supplementary Note 1). A representative XSTM topography of the metal–dielectric interface is shown in Fig. 3c, whereas spatially resolved XSTM-STS measurements acquired at sub-0.5 nm intervals from the interface into the dielectric are presented in Fig. 3d. Amorphous HfO2 has pronounced in-gap states near the band edges, particularly close to the interface, indicating a high density of charge-trapping centres. By contrast, no discernible in-gap states are detected in A-TiO2, supporting its intrinsically low trap density.

Moreover, current-mode deep-level transient spectroscopy (I-DLTS) reveals distinct trap characteristics at 1L-MoS2/dielectric interfaces (Fig. 3e). 1L-MoS2/HfO2 has a shallow trap (0.221 eV below Ec) with a large capture cross-section (σn = 1.40 × 10−13 cm2). Conversely, 1L-MoS2/A-TiO2 shows a deeper trap at 0.293 eV below Ec with a capture cross-section that is three orders of magnitude smaller (σn = 6.40 × 10−17 cm2), substantially suppressing trapping (Supplementary Note 2). The close agreement between XSTM-STS and I-DLTS measurements indicates that shallow, Coulomb-attractive traps dominate the 1L-MoS2/HfO2 interface, whereas deeper, near-neutral traps in A-TiO2   exhibit substantially lower trapping probability. The influence of dielectric quality is further illustrated in Fig. 3f, which compares the transfer characteristics of WSe2 p-FETs fabricated with A-TiO2 and amorphous HfO2 gate dielectrics. The A-TiO2-gated device has clean unipolar p-type behaviour across the entire gate sweep; however, the HfO2-gated device shows pronounced bipolar transport, incompatible with robust CMOS operation. This contrast indicates that the bipolar response is linked to defect-induced Fermi-level modulation associated with in-gap states in the amorphous dielectric (Supplementary Note 3). These findings underscore the critical importance of using high-quality dielectrics with low-trap density to achieve stable, unipolar p-type operation in WSe2 FETs.

The stable and high-performance A-TiO2-gated 2D FETs motivate us to further demonstrate their scalable vertical integration into complementary field-effect transistors (CFETs) (Fig. 4a). Fabrication begins with MoS2 n-FET arrays, using buried gold electrodes as source and drain contacts and single-crystalline A-TiO2 as the top-gate dielectric. A vertical CMOS architecture is then constructed by stacking 2L-WSe2/A-TiO2 p-FET arrays directly above the n-type tier, sharing a common Pt gate electrode. After vertically interconnecting the drain electrodes of n- and p-FETs through the via-metal, where the output voltage (Vout) is measured, the CFET inverters are realized (the schematic structure is shown in Fig. 4b; refer to Extended Data Fig. 6 for detailed fabrication steps). Figure 4c shows the cross-sectional HRTEM images acquired at the channel region of a representative CFET inverter, revealing uniformly flat layers with atomically sharp vdW interfaces between the 2D semiconductors and the A-TiO2 gate dielectrics. An overview cross-sectional HRTEM image of the complete CFET stack, illustrating the vertical alignment of the top p-FET and bottom n-FET tiers, is provided in Extended Data Fig. 7.

Note that VM = Vdd/2 occurs when n-FET and p-FET are well matched—a condition essential for maximizing noise margins and minimizing static power consumption14,15,56,57,58,59. h, The optical micrograph of CFET-based NAND (left) and NOR (right) gates. The corresponding output characteristics are shown for supply voltages ranging from 0.5 V to 1.0 V.

The transfer curves of the bottom n-FETs and top p-FETs (Lch = 1 μm) measured from 16 CFETs are shown in Fig. 4d, exhibiting nearly symmetric behavior and limited device-to-device variation. Note that the voltage transfer characteristic (VTC) curves shown for the CFET inverters exclude abnormal devices (Supplementary Note 4). The yield of the CFET inverters is approximately 50% (25 functional devices out of 50 fabricated devices) and requires further engineering improvement. The standard deviations of normalized Ion are 21.8% for the n-FETs and 23.9% for the p-FETs. The average Vth is 0.9 V for the n-FETs and −1.1 V for the p-FETs, confirming enhancement-mode operation for both device types, which is essential for low-power logic applications. Both n- and p-FETs have steep subthreshold slopes, indicating high transconductance ( gm, defined as the change in drain current with respect to gate voltage, ∆Ids/∆Vgs) and transconductance efficiency (gm/Ids), which are essential for achieving large voltage gain in CFET inverters. Consistently, both device types maintain Ion/Ioff ratios exceeding 107 over a range of Vds while preserving a minimum subthreshold swing of about 75 mV dec–1 (Supplementary Fig. 19), enabling efficient inverter operation at reduced supply voltage (Vdd) with low power consumption. Figure 4e displays representative VTCs of the CFET inverters, demonstrating excellent full-rail logic swing across a range of Vdd from 0.1 V to 1 V. The voltage gain increases progressively with Vdd, from 12 V/V at 0.25 V to a peak value of 89 V/V at 1 V. Remarkably, even at the minimum Vdd of 0.1 V, the inverter maintains a gain value exceeding the minimum threshold (1 V/V) for functional logic operation37, highlighting the potential of this CFET architecture for ultra-low-voltage, energy-efficient circuits. Supplementary Fig. 20 summarizes the voltage gain, static power consumption (Pstatic) and estimated noise margins (NML, low-level noise margin; NMH, high-level noise margin) as functions of Vdd, extracted from 16 individual CFET inverters. Owing to the crystalline nature of the high-κ dielectric and well-matched characteristics of n/p-FETs, the CFET inverters had ultralow gate and channel leakage currents during operation, resulting in exceptionally low Pstatic. At Vdd = 0.25 V, Pstatic is measured to be 38 fW, and even at Vdd = 1 V it remains as low as 1 pW. As summarized in Fig. 4f, the achieved Pstatic is the lowest reported among 2D material-based CMOS inverters, while simultaneously maintaining high gain.

Figure 4g compares the voltage gain values versus switch point (VM/Vdd), where VM denotes the input voltage at which Vout equals Vin. A switching point near 0.5 is critical for maximizing noise margins and ensuring symmetric logic operation. The CFET inverters demonstrated here not only achieve high voltage gains but also maintain VM/Vdd values close to the ideal 0.5. To further evaluate the noise tolerance of our CFET inverters, we estimated the noise margin (NM% = NML% + NMH%) values from the VTCs for 16 individual devices. The average NM% values are 67.5%, 82.5%, 87.5% and 89.2% at Vdd values of 0.25 V, 0.5 V, 0.75 V and 1 V, respectively (Supplementary Fig. 20), exceeding previously reported CFET implementations (Extended Data Table 1).

Beyond inverter operation, logic gate networks, including NAND and NOR gates, were implemented using CFET-based pull-up and pull-down configurations comprising two p-FETs and two n-FETs (Fig. 4h and Supplementary Fig. 21). Both logic gates operate reliably at a low Vdd of 0.5 V, demonstrating the feasibility of CFET-based logic beyond single-inverter circuits. The thermal stability of A-TiO2-integrated CFETs was evaluated at both material and device levels (Supplementary Note 5). The results support that the A-TiO2 dielectric and its interfaces with TMD channels retain electrical and crystallographic integrity under  back-end-of-line (BEOL) thermal conditions (up to 400 °C). However, extended high-temperature exposure beyond conventional limits causes noticeable device degradation.

Furthermore, the electrical performance of short-channel CFET inverters with about 50 nm channel lengths in both the bottom- and top-tier FETs was also evaluated (Extended Data Fig. 8a). The transfer characteristics of the p-FET and n-FET show well-matched threshold voltages and on-currents (Extended Data Fig. 8b). This electrical symmetry enables a high inverter voltage gain (gain = 97 V/V at Vdd = 1 V). The improvement is attributed to the higher switching current enabled by the short channels, as illustrated in the VTC and corresponding gain curve in Extended Data Fig. 8c,d. As expected, the static power consumption of these short-channel devices is higher than that of long-channel (Lch = 1 μm) CFETs, as a result of increased short-circuit current and Ioff during switching (Extended Data Fig. 8e). Further work on integrating Vth-tuning techniques is needed to achieve the critical balance of high gain and low power consumption in our CFET technology. Furthermore, we estimate dynamic power (Pdyn) (Supplementary Note 6), where the analysis indicates that the scaled CFET achieves a 39% reduction in dynamic power (Pdyn ≈ 230.3 nW, Vdd = 0.5 V), compared with the long-channel counterpart (Pdyn ≈ 378.3 nW, Vdd = 0.5 V). This improvement arises from reduced intrinsic and Miller capacitances associated with the scaled geometry, which outweighs the additional parasitic coupling introduced by the vertical stacking38,39.

In summary, this work demonstrates a 3-inch freestanding A-TiO2 membrane as a gate dielectric that delivers exceptional thickness uniformity and favourable dielectric metrics. The atomically clean interface formed between A-TiO2 and 2D materials enables low subthreshold swing, record-low hysteresis and well-balanced enhancement-mode operation for both n- and p-type transistors. Building on this gate-stack platform, vertically stacked CFET inverter arrays have high voltage gain, wide noise margins and ultralow static power consumption. Density functional theory (DFT) combined with NEGF (NEGF-DFT) simulations further project that the proposed 2D CFET architecture can be scaled to the 1-nm node while sustaining stable operation (Supplementary Note 7). Together, these results establish wafer-scale single-crystal high-κ dielectrics integrated with 2D semiconductors as viable and promising platforms for energy-efficient logic technologies, positioning them as compelling candidates for the post-silicon electronics roadmap.

The AlO2-terminated surface of single-crystalline 3-inch LaAlO3 (001) substrates was prepared by wet etching of LaAlO3 (001) for 30 s with dilute HCl (pH ≈ 4.5), followed by 1,000 °C annealing in a pure oxygen atmosphere. The atomically sharp step and terraces of substrates were examined by AFM. The SrTiO3, Sr3Al2O6 and A-TiO2 films were grown by pulsed laser deposition using a 248-nm krypton fluoride excimer laser with a laser fluence of 48 mJ cm–2. A laser-scanning system capable of depositing films on wafers up to 4-inch in diameter was used, in which a linear translation stage, rather than a galvanometer, was used to scan the laser beam across a rotating target. This configuration eliminates optical distortions and maintains consistent ablation conditions, thereby ensuring uniform film growth. The SrTiO3 buffer layer and water-soluble Sr3Al2O6 layers were deposited at 850 °C with an oxygen partial pressure (\({p}_{{{\rm{O}}}_{2}}\)) of 1 × 10−6 torr. The in situ RHEED patterns indicated the highly crystalline nature for the as-grown A-TiO2 layer, respectively (Extended Data Fig. 1a). The epitaxial growth of the A-TiO2 layer on the Sr3Al2O6 thin film was then conducted at 800 °C and \({p}_{{{\rm{O}}}_{2}}\) = 1 × 10−4 torr. On the completion of film deposition, the sample was cooled down to room temperature under \({p}_{{{\rm{O}}}_{2}}\) = 1 × 10−1 torr to prevent non-stoichiometry in A-TiO2 film.

The 1L-MoS2 film was synthesized via a CVD method on C/M sapphire substrates (supplied by Crystal-wise Technology), which had undergone surface reconstruction. Molybdenum trioxide (MoO3, 99.5%) and sulfur (S, 99.5%) powders (both from Sigma-Aldrich) were positioned in separate zones of a quartz tube furnace. A heating belt regulated the sulfur evaporation at 160–180 °C, whereas the substrate and MoO3 were heated to 700 °C. An argon gas flow facilitated the transport of vapourized precursors. The growth process lasted 15 min, after which the system was allowed to cool naturally to room temperature. The 2L-WSe2 film was provided by Nexstrom, where the samples were grown by CVD methods. The transfer procedures of 1L-MoS2 and 2L-WSe2 follow the common polymethyl-methacrylate-assisted wet transfer method.

X-ray diffraction measurements were conducted using a Rigaku SmartLab thin-film XRD system with a rotating copper anode X-ray source. The dislocation density (\(\rho \)) is evaluated using the Vannas (Halliwell–Hirsch) model:

where \(\beta \) is the FWHM in radians and \(b\) is the Burgers vector. The surface morphologies were examined by AFM (Bruker Dimension Icon SPM). The film thickness uniformity was measured by an ellipsometer (J.A. Woollam RC2). Raman and Photoluminescence spectra of MoS2 and WSe2 were collected in a confocal Raman microscopy system (WITec alpha 300 R) with a 532-nm laser. The cross-sectional STM measurement was conducted under ultrahigh vacuum (5 × 10−11 torr) at room temperature. Plan-view dark-field TEM image and SAED pattern of A-TiO2 membrane were captured using a Thermo Scientific Talos F200X STEM at 200 kV from a top-view sample suspended on a holey carbon grid. Cross-section lamellas for LaAlO3//SrTiO3//Sr3Al2O6//A-TiO2 heterostructure, single FET and CFET devices were prepared with a focused-ion-beam system (Thermo Scientific Helios 5 CX). Cross-section STEM images and EDS mapping were conducted by the same STEM system at 200 kV. The surface topography and structure of CFET logic gates were examined by SEM (Zeiss Sigma 300 VP).

For MIM capacitors, the A-TiO2 membranes were transferred onto Au-coated Si substrates; subsequently, 10 nm Ti and 80 nm Au electrodes were fabricated through the shadow mask by electron-beam evaporation. For ALD-grown amorphous dielectric oxides, we used trimethylaluminum and water as the precursors for Al2O3 deposition, whereas tetrakis (dimethylamido) hafnium and water served as the precursors for HfO2, with the growth temperature of 150 °C. For FET fabrication (Supplementary Fig. 8), the A-TiO2 membranes and 1L-MoS2/2L-WSe2 layers were sequentially transferred onto a Ti/Pt (1 nm/8 nm) local back-gate array. The channel area was defined using electron-beam lithography followed by O2 reactive-ion etching (10 mTorr, 100 W). After patterning the source/drain regions using electron-beam lithography, Sb/Au (20 nm/40 nm) and Pt/Au (5 nm/15 nm) contacts were deposited to form n-type 1L-MoS2 and p-type 2L-WSe2 FETs, respectively. The metals were deposited using thermal and e-beam evaporation, and the chamber pressure was maintained at around 10−8 Torr throughout the metal deposition process. For CFET devices (Extended Data Fig. 6), a 12-nm Au layer was first deposited on the substrate to serve as the bottom contact for the n-FET. A 1L-MoS2 film was transferred and patterned, followed by the transfer of an A-TiO2 membrane as the gate dielectric. A 10-nm Pt mid-gate was then defined on A-TiO2 to serve as the shared gate for both bottom n-FET and top p-FET. The top device was then completed by sequential transfer of a second A-TiO2 membrane and a 2L-WSe2 film, which was intentionally adopted to improve device-to-device uniformity and process tolerance during multilayer CFET fabrication, supported by independent statistical comparison of 1L-WSe2 and 2L-WSe2 devices (Supplementary Note 8). To remove surface polymer residue, a mild O2 plasma treatment (15 W, 20 s) and hot-acetone vapour (80 °C, 30 min) were applied after transferring the A-TiO2 and 2D material layers, respectively. After electron-beam lithography alignment of the active regions, 5 nm Pt/20 nm Au were deposited to form the p-FET contacts. Finally, the CFET inverter was formed by interconnecting the two pads respectively from n- and p-FETs through a via opening defined by O2/SF6 inductively coupled plasma etching, followed by Au metallization. The same via process was used for NAND and NOR logic demonstrations.

Electrical characterization of the devices was performed using a Keysight B1500A semiconductor parameter analyser mounted in a closed-cycle cryogenic probe station (at a base pressure of about 10−6 Torr). Capacitance measurements were conducted with the Keysight E5288A C-V Measurement System integrated into the B1500A platform. All devices were measured under vacuum conditions within a probe station featuring a shielded enclosure to reduce electromagnetic interference. The \(|\Delta {V}_{H}|\) extracted from Supplementary Figs. 16 and 17 is calculated via

Where \({V}_{\mathrm{th},\mathrm{forward}}\) and \({V}_{\mathrm{th},\mathrm{reverse}}\) denote the Vth extracted from the forward and backward transfer sweeps, respectively. \({D}_{\mathrm{it}}\) at the channel-dielectric interface is calculated using the expression:

where \({C}_{\mathrm{ox}}\) is the gate dielectric capacitance obtained from MIM capacitance measurements (Extended Data Fig. 2), \(q\) is the elementary charge, \({k}_{{\rm{B}}}\) is the Boltzmann constant and \(T\) is the absolute temperature. Pstatic is calculated as \({{V}}_{{\rm{dd}}}\times ({I}_{{{\rm{Static}}}_{{\rm{low}}}}+{I}_{{{\rm{Static}}}_{{\rm{high}}}})/2\) in the static regime (Vin = 0 V or Vin = Vdd).

Bias-temperature instability measurements were performed at room temperature by applying gate biases of –1 V and +2 V, respectively, for 1,000 s. After removal of the stress bias, Vth recovery was monitored through transfer measurements at Vds = 1 V. The same extraction criterion was used throughout, and the Vth shift was calculated relative to the initial value as ΔVth = Vth,t – Vth,0.

The transport properties of the 1L-MoS2 and 2L-WSe2 FETs were investigated using DFT combined with the NEGF formalism, as implemented in the QuantumATK package60. Here, \({V}_{\mathrm{gs}}\) and \({V}_{\mathrm{dd}}\) were set to be 0.6 V. All calculations were performed using linear combination of atomic orbitals (LCAO) basis set with high accuracy and PseudoDojo pseudopotential61. The exchange-correlation functional was treated at the GGA-PBE level. For the MoS2 DG-FET, a 15 × 1 × 173 Monkhorst–Pack k-point grid is used. For the 2L-WSe2 DG-FET, a 33 × 1 × 165 grid is adopted and vdW-D3 correction is used for vdW interaction62. The gate length of both devices is set to 10 nm. Two gate dielectrics are examined for electrostatic control: SiO2 with a permittivity of 3.9 and thickness of 0.9 nm, and TiO2 with a high-κ value of 25 and thickness of 5.8 nm. The atomic compensation-charge method is used to control the doping distribution in the source and drain extensions.

Relevant data supporting the key findings of this study are available in the article and the Supplementary Information. All raw data generated during the current study are available from the corresponding authors on reasonable request.

#1440. Taking instructions from a schoolboy and showing class at half-pace... William Saliba made impressive injury comeback for Arsenal Under-21s - now he faces fight to take Ezri Konsa's spot, writes ISAAN KHAN

Published: 06:24 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 06:28 EST, 11 November 2026

It was a scene straight out of Will Ferrell's Elf. In the middle of Arsenal's Under-21 team huddle stood William Saliba, all 6ft 4in of him, towering over his teenage team-mates as 17-year-old captain Marli Salmon delivered his pre-match rallying cry.

One of the world's finest defenders was taking instructions from a schoolboy.

For the hundreds of Arsenal supporters who had descended on Boreham Wood's Meadow Park on Sunday, it was an extraordinary sight. Four months after suffering a back injury in France's World Cup semi-final defeat by Spain, Saliba was finally back on a football pitch.

But his carefully managed 45-minute appearance in a 5-2 victory over Aston Villa's Under-21s marked the beginning of another challenge. Saliba must now win back a place in an Arsenal defence which, remarkably, has barely missed him.

That is largely down to Ezri Konsa, the £55million summer signing from Aston Villa who has been so impressive in Saliba's absence that Mikel Arteta faces a genuine selection dilemma.

Saliba and Gabriel have been Arsenal's established central defensive partnership since the opening day of the 2022-23 season. But Konsa, arguably Arsenal's outstanding defender this term, has made a compelling case to keep his place.

William Saliba towered over his teenage team-mates and played 45 minutes on Sunday

His performance in the 1-0 victory at Liverpool, Arsenal's first win at Anfield in 14 years, was particularly impressive. He won every ground duel, made 14 defensive contributions and completed eight clearances, leading the match statistics in all three categories. Liverpool failed to register a shot on target.

It was precisely the sort of performance that has given Arteta something to think about. And the Arsenal manager is understood to have challenged Konsa to fight for his place rather than simply make way for the returning Frenchman.

There is another solution. Konsa can operate at right back, a position he has occupied for both Villa and England, including during the summer's World Cup. That would allow Arteta to restore the Saliba-Gabriel partnership without sacrificing a player who has become such an important part of Arsenal's defence. For now, however, there will be no rush.

Saliba's injury history explains why Arsenal have been so careful. In 2022-23, another back problem kept him out for 97 days and contributed significantly to the collapse of a title challenge that had seen the club spend 248 days at the top of the Premier League.

Arsenal have since finished runners-up again and finally claimed the title last summer, but the lessons of that earlier setback have not been forgotten.

Leading back specialists were consulted over Saliba's latest injury before the club settled on a conservative rehabilitation programme, deliberately extending his recovery rather than risking another setback.

He returned to full first-team training last Tuesday, ahead of Arsenal's 2-1 victory over Slavia Prague, but Sunday's appearance represented his first competitive action since July. His absence from France's squad during the international break should allow Arsenal to continue building his fitness without interruption.

And there was plenty to suggest that the long wait has done little to diminish his quality.

The Frenchman is building up his fitness after four months on the sidelines

Saliba faces a tough test to try and break up the partnership formed by Gabriel and Ezri Konsa

Playing comfortably within himself, Saliba repeatedly strolled past opponents before threading passes through the Villa midfield. At times he ventured so far forward after set-pieces that supporters began joking about whether he fancied himself as a centre-forward.

Even at half-pace, the gulf between a world-class defender and academy football was obvious.

Yet it was Saliba's interaction with his young team-mates that provided some of the afternoon's most revealing moments.

Throughout the first half he could be heard directing Salmon, shouting 'man on,' 'high, high' and 'well done, Marli' as he guided his teenage defensive partner through the game.

When Arsenal scored their opening goal, Salmon initially stayed back rather than joining the celebrations. Saliba promptly ordered him forward to enjoy the moment.

Marli Salmon, pictured laying a wreath for Remembrance Day, was the one barking out instructions and seeing Saliba (left) among the youngsters was an extraordinary sight

It was a small gesture but typical of the interest Saliba has taken in Arsenal's younger players during his rehabilitation.

He is understood to have spent time asking about their families and offering advice about life in professional football.

One particular message has been the importance of looking after their parents if they are fortunate enough to make a successful career in the game. The affection is clearly mutual.

Children clamoured for autographs as Saliba arrived and departed, while Arsenal had prepared for the unusual attention surrounding an Under 21 fixture.

Large QR codes directing spectators to the team line-up had been displayed around the ground and a member of the first-team security staff accompanied Saliba between the dressing room and the pitch.

His afternoon was meticulously choreographed. At half-time, his work completed, he disappeared into the changing rooms before leaving through a side exit.

Saliba made his comeback for Arsenal's Under 21 side after a long injury absence

The 45 minutes will have provided reassurance to Arteta and Arsenal's medical staff, as well as a memorable afternoon for the teenagers who shared the pitch with him. For Saliba, though, the real work is only beginning.

Few would have imagined when he suffered his injury in July that he might return to find his place under threat. Konsa's performances have changed that calculation.

Arsenal have their defensive cornerstone back. Now Arteta must decide what to do with him.

#1439. The unexpected email that led to Bukayo Saka's Socrates Award win at the Ballon d'Or: Inside Arsenal star's secret humanitarian work after his surprise win at London ceremony

Published: 08:07 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 08:13 EST, 11 November 2026

The sight of Bukayo Saka hobbling down the red carpet at the Ballon d'Or ceremony came as a surprise. Only those closest to him knew why he was there, and the years of toil that led to this moment.

While his England team-mate Harry Kane claimed the night's top on-pitch prize, Saka – who had suffered a thigh injury just days before against Kane's Bayern Munich – was at the London Palladium to collect the Socrates Award for his humanitarian work.

Joining a roll of honour that includes previous winners Vinicius Junior, Sadio Mane and Luis Enrique, Saka walked onto the stage, reached into his suit pocket and read a letter from a 14-year-old boy in Rwanda whose eyesight had been restored through his charity work.

Now, Daily Mail Sport can reveal the scale of the Arsenal star's involvement over the last four years with the BigShoe charity, which funds operations, feeds children and helps with disaster relief across the world. From restoring the eyesight of that 14-year-old in Rwanda to helping provide life-saving procedures for 120 children in Nigeria, Saka's impact goes far beyond the stadiums he dazzles in.

And this is no passive act of philanthropy. BigShoe president Valerie Fiesser's phone is often inundated with messages from Saka when the charity is delivering projects in poverty-stricken countries such as Nigeria and Rwanda. Many of the project ideas come from the 25-year-old himself.

'Bukayo is really, really productive,' Fiesser tells Daily Mail Sport. 'He is really pushing how he wants to help. I think for him it is never fast enough to help. Sometimes Bukayo comes up with projects and he says, "Shouldn't we help here?" So he is really interested in it. It is not like he is just sending money and saying, "OK, nice, we'll do a project in Nigeria".

Bukayo Saka was handed the Ballon d'Or Socrates Award for his humanitarian work last month

Saka has worked with BigShoe charity for years - helping those in poverty-stricken countries

In 2023, Saka donated 50 containers to help provide shelter for 255 people impacted by the devastating earthquake in Morocco

'When we are on the ground, he is texting, "Is everything alright? Is everybody safe? Are all the children safe? Which services do we have? Can I see pictures? Send me pictures, send me pictures, send me pictures!"

BigShoe, a German-based charity founded during the 2006 World Cup, began years ago by funding life-changing surgery for Nourisson, a young girl from Togo born with a cleft lip and palate. The Togo national team, playing at their first World Cup, were based in the city of Wangen im Allgau, which brought the story to prominence in Germany.

The charity is now a worldwide network of football stars, fans and partners, with more than 10,000 children around the globe having benefitted via projects ranging from medical supplies to shelter and food. The organisation has also worked with Antonio Rudiger, Paul Pogba and Saka's ex-Arsenal team-mates Mesut Ozil and Oleksandr Zinchenko.

Fiesser vividly remembers how Saka first got in touch, in early 2022.

'He just really randomly wrote us an email,' she says. 'He asked us if we can help together in Nigeria after seeing a project of another soccer player. He said, "I want to help children, I want to help people and can we do something". (It was) really just random.'

That initial conversation quickly developed into a project in late 2022 which funded 120 life-changing medical operations for children in Nigeria. Some of the youngsters were suffering from brain tumours, while others required treatment for hernias.

'This was an incredible project because it was the first project in Nigeria together with him,' she says. 'It was really life-changing for the children because some had a brain tumour, some had hernia problems.'

Saka has since helped support healthcare check-ups for more than 580 children in Rwanda and provide disaster relief after devastating earthquakes in Morocco and Turkey, while his involvement has extended far beyond financial backing.

The charity is now a worldwide network of football stars, fans and partners, with more than 10,000 kids having benefitted via projects ranging from medical supplies to shelter and food

'We did a disaster relief where we provided homes for the earthquake victims in Morocco and Turkey and he was asking questions like, "Do they have electricity there?"' she says.

'He is really thinking, "Is it worth it, does it make sense to do this, or is it just putting the container and then the people do not have water and they cannot live there?" So he is really, really smart. And yes, I think he is an amazing human.

'It was never about him. It was always about the children and how we can help. It was never like, "OK, we are talking to one of the best players of the world." I think he is raised like this. His family made him the man he is now.

'I think he is raised like this, that you have to be a good human being and to help others and just have an impact in life.'

Saka and his family are directly involved in the projects, identifying communities in need and deciding exactly how support should be delivered. His mother, Adenike, is a key figure.

'We decide together where we can help, how we can help and then we actually help together,' Fiesser says. 'Me and his mother WhatsApp, call regularly. She has played a big part and is a driving force.

'Three months ago we renovated a school in Rwanda and we provided them with water filters for clean drinking water. We also built girls' changing rooms, a new soccer pitch and a new library. Bukayo's family was on the ground, twice.

'We decided after we saw that the families are really hungry in this area to do food packages. It is our next project in November and December.

'He (Saka) really wants to make a difference. He wants to change lives.'

While Saka will continue to chase trophies in Arsenal red and England white, his greatest legacy may ultimately be measured in the lives he has changed far beyond the football pitch.

#1438. Late Benjamin Goal Secures Deserved Point For Under-21s

A superb late equaliser from Omari Benjamin secured a deserved 1-1 draw for Everton's Under-21s away at Crystal Palace in Premier League 2.

Benjamin's turn past the last man and chipped finish ensured a share of the spoils for Dave Hughes' side, who had gone behind to Seb Williams' goal early in the second half but always looked threatening and could have won it late on.

Academy graduate Tom Davies also featured for the Under-21s, coming on as a second-half substitute as the Academy continues to support the midfielder with his fitness while he looks to secure a professional contract elsewhere.

Four changes were made from the side that defeated Tamworth 3-2 in the National League Cup in midweek. Ezra Carrington returned to the starting XI at left-back with Melvin Matos slotting into central midfield, while Under-18s players John Dodds and Harry Brookes were both given starts in central defence and attacking midfield respectively.

Chances were at somewhat of a premium in the early stages although the Toffees were working the ball nicely in possession. In the 10th minute Brookes burst into the box after striker Ceiran Loney won possession back in the final third, but as he fired at goal Brookes saw his effort blocked by a last-ditch sliding challenge from Palace captain George King.

The danger man for Palace looked to be Dean Benamar and the winger twice sent efforts at goal in the first half, drilling one effort narrowly wide in the 18th minute before forcing a fine stop from Toffees keeper Fraser Barnsley eight minutes later.

Everton responded well with Braiden Graham curling one effort high and wide from 18 yards and skipper Will Tamen heading narrowly wide from a corner on the stroke of half-time, while Palace rattled the crossbar through Amaari Sealey's effort.

The period immediately after the restart gave a hint as to how the second half would play out. Palace immediately got on the attack but could not find a way to goal, and the Toffees countered superbly as a result, with Loney being played through one-on-one only for keeper Lucca Benetton to produce an excellent stop to deny the Scottish youth international.

That lifted Palace and shortly after he had seen a flicked effort from eight yards fly wide of the far post, Williams made no mistake with his second effort just past the hour, poking the ball past Barnsley after King's flick-on into the box split the defence.

King would then rattle the woodwork five minutes later as Palace looked for a second goal, but the Toffees defended manfully and gradually began to take control of the game. Substitute Jonathan Nsangou thought he had won a penalty in the 77th minute when he was brought down after surging into the box from the right channel, but the referee gave a free kick on the edge and Benjamin headed wide from Graham's delivery.

But there was still time for an equaliser and it duly came with five minutes of regular time to play. Luis Gardner stepped out from centre-back and played an arrowed forward pass to Benjamin, who flicked the ball with the outside of his foot around King before racing onto it and into the box.

King and Benetton both tried to challenge the Everton man but it was no use – Benjamin dinked the ball eloquently over the on-rushing goalkeeper and it nestled in the back of the net.

If either side was going to win it late on, it looked more likely to be the Toffees, who sent a series of deliveries into the box but could not find that final shot on goal, and the points were shared in South London.

Speaking after the game, Head of Academy Player Development Dave Hughes told evertonfc.com: "We felt (we deserved a point at least). We had probably four or five really good chances with counters in the final third, and maybe didn’t get our shots away cleanly. They got some excellent blocks in and around the box.

"We definitely felt we didn’t deserve to lose and I'm sure they’d say similar. For the first 15-20 minutes we controlled large parts of the game, in the second half it became more open. We showed great character and resilience to stay in the game after going 1-0 down and that’s one thing you’d give the lads credit for – in every game, if we’ve gone behind, we’ve found a way to get back into it. We had a good spell at the end where we maybe could have finished it.

"It's a great finish from Omari, outstanding actually, over the keeper, and the turn as well.

"It's pleasing to have got so many of the Under-18s on. John Dodds started, Malik and Jonathan Nsangou came on, Harry Brookes played – all-in-all it's a very good afternoon. A result we definitely warranted and plenty of positives to take. It was great to see Will Tamen step up his time again from Tuesday night as well, we're really pleased for him.

"We're pleased with how the group are going about their work. Performances have been consistent and I feel as though the lads are giving a good account of themselves. We’ve been difficult to play against at times, but of course we can be more so.

"Tom’s an unbelievable professional. All the staff and players have witnessed that he’s a model professional in the way that he goes about his work. He’s shown the players, if they needed it, what a top professional looks like. How he trains, how he conducts himself. He’s given guidance and advice to the younger players. He’s been a credit to himself and to the Academy."

#1437. Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s new-look midfield

This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

“It’s nice to keep a clean sheet and obviously win the game,” Carrick said. “Some of the football we played was really good – dangerous on the transition. The result looks comfortable, but it wasn’t always like that but we did a lot of good things.

United probably could not have asked for a softer return to Champions League football. Atlético Madrid at the Wanda Metropolitano next month will certainly be a very different beast, but it was a rewarding first 45 minutes all the same that paved the way for Carrick to ring the changes ahead of the derby.

Already leading 1-0, two goals shortly before the interval changed the complexion of the game and effectively extinguished any flickering hopes Sabah had of a gargantuan upset.

Founded just nine years ago, Sabah had navigated four qualifying rounds that began on July 7 just to reach this stage.

Throw in the fact Valdas Dambrauskas, their Lithuanian manager, got his break in coaching with the Manchester United Soccer Schools 20 years ago, and it is quite the heartwarming tale.

But there is not much sentiment at this level and, given time and space, United punished their inexperience and carelessness.

Carrick will not read too much into the performance. City will be an entirely different proposition and it will be interesting to see whether he goes for a two-man midfield with Bruno Fernandes deployed as an advanced No 10, or perhaps operates with a midfield three and adjusts his attack.

Either way, Mainoo will be central to the game plan.

It is hard to believe the England midfielder missed most of pre-season after reporting back late following the World Cup, because he has barely missed a beat in his last three outings, even if his team-mates have not always hummed to his tune.

There is so much to like about Mainoo. His manipulation of space, how he never looks under duress, even when hounded, and his vision on the ball. There was one lovely angled ball over the top here, after United had worked the space well, that released Fernandes in behind. His cross was cut out before Sesko could tap in.

Mainoo’s work off the ball has improved enormously, too. There were numerous instances here of him making a timely intervention or nicking the ball away at the right moment to recover possession.United have spent £155m reconfiguring their midfield, but Mainoo will be a constant. “He’s a fantastic player, it’s pretty obvious to see,” Carrick said. “He has a massive influence on our games. He is a real joy to have, he wants to improve, he wants to listen and it’s great to see.”

Kobbie Mainoo completed 81/83 passes, 6/6 accurate long balls and 10 passes into final third on his full Champions League debut ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/NK9BIGvc4m

It will certainly be interesting to see how Carrick’s new-look midfield shapes up against City’s own revamped one in the form of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

“There are some good connections and we have played some good football through the middle of the pitch,” Carrick added. “A lot of it is on wavelength and understanding of where each other wants the ball. We haven’t had the perfect start but there are really good signs.”

Carrick was suitably confident to withdraw Youri Tielemans at half-time and bring on Mason Mount, who was having a good pre-season before his familiar injury jinx hit, and he will have been pleased to see Sesko on the scoresheet again. “He definitely offers a different kind of threat,” Carrick said. “There are not many who can give us what Ben does with his physicality, playing on the last line. It’s great to have him back.”

Sesko’s goal, rounding the goalkeeper to slot home from Bryan Mbeumo’s pass after line-breaking balls from Mainoo and Fernandes, capped off a quick-fire three minutes when Sabah were unpicked. Before then, Cunha had picked out Tielemans’s burst into the penalty area, from where he pulled the ball back for Fernandes to coolly finish.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

United had taken the lead when Kaheem Parris paid the price for a misplaced pass straight to Mbeumo, from which the ball was moved at pace between Sesko, Fernandes and Patrick Dorgu to tee up Cunha to score.

Dorgu was starting here at left-back with Shaw rested with one eye on City. It was an early glimpse of how Carrick is going to have to manage the minutes of his only recognised senior left-back, who is not going to be able to play every few days.

Carrick prefers Dorgu further up the pitch and it remains to be seen if he trusts the Dane at left-back in bigger games than this.

With City having played in Porto on Tuesday and had a little extra rest time, the United manager will have been pleased he got the chance to withdraw several key players early. He was even able to give a rare run-out to Joshua Zirkzee and it was the Dutchman who helped to force the fourth goal.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Fernandes’s quick free-kick caught out Sabah and Zirkzee back-heeled the ball goalwards. It bounced off Aden McCarthy and from there goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov got himself in a dreadful spin, unable to locate the ball by which point Martínez had blasted it in from a yard out.

“Nice to have a clean sheet and obviously win the game. Some of our attacking play was fantastic. We were dangerous in transition, defended well in the most part. The result looks comfortable but it was not as easy as that. Kobbie [Mainoo] is a fantastic player, it is pretty obvious to see. He has a massive influence on our game and a real joy to have. Through the middle of the pitch, we have played some good football at times and we can get better. There are some good signs which we have shown tonight. The confidence is there, like at Everton on Sunday for large spells, just took a hit there at the end with the result. It is always nice to win. Another big one on Sunday.”

81 - Kobbie Mainoo completed the most passes in Manchester United's 4-0 win over Sabah (81).It was the most by an Englishman for the Red Devils in a UEFA Champions League match since Michael Carrick in February 2014 vs Olympiakos (89).Mentor. pic.twitter.com/59wSvQydOG

The final whistle is blown at Old Trafford and Manchester United claim a 4-0 victory on their return to the Champions League. Goals from Cunha, Fernandes, Sesko and Martinez give Michael Carrick’s side three points in their opening game of the competition. Debutants Sabah return home with nothing and no goals, despite some decent chances to get a goal.

A number of empty seats at Old Trafford are becoming visible as some home fans have seen enough, knowing their side is going to win.

Sabah have had a few chances to come away from their Champions League debut with a goal but have wasted some great chances, including one just now. Mickels delivers a lovely cross from the left, which perfectly picks out Mbina, but his header goes just over the bar.

Mickels wasted a glorious chance in the first half and he comes close to goal a now but drags his shot just wide of the far post from the left side of the box.

How on earth have the officials missed that one? Cunha catches Almeida on the leg and it should be at least a booking but the officials do not see it, despite the linesman being not far away. Cunha is very lucky as that was a nasty challenge.

Sabah would love to at the very least send their travelling fans back to Azerbaijan with a goal on their Champions League debut. You do wonder how different the game could have been had Mickels not missed a sitter that would have seen Sabah make it 1-1.

Michael Carrick is going to make his final two changes of the night as youngsters Lacey and Amass come on.

A bit of a soft goal for Sabah to concede. Fernandes clips in a free-kick into the Sabah box which picks out the run of Zirkzee. The Dutchman’s backheel is blocked and Sabah should then deal with the danger. However, Sabah make an absolute mess of things and their keeper Pokatilov has no idea where the ball is, allowing Martinez to nick in and smash the ball into the net.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Lepinjica is the first Sabah player into the book tonight for a cynical trip on Mount.

Zirkzee, only just on the pitch, shoots from range but it is straight down the throat of Pokatilov.

Puchacz takes the free-kick from just over 25 yards out and strikes it well but the effort is just off target.

Perhaps with the Manchester derby on Sunday in mind, Michael Carrick is going to make a double change. Zirkzee and Santos replace Sesko and Mainoo.

Dorgu is the first player into the book tonight. Lepinjica spots the run of Parris into the right channel and plays a clever pas forward. Dorgu cynically brings Parris down and is rightly booked.

The visitors are making a change as Parris is replaced by Isaev.

Manchester United come close to a fourth and Cunha his second. The home side work it well near the Sabah penalty area with a couple of clever flicks and passes before Cunha has an effort saved by Pokatilov to his left.

Mazraoui receives it out in space on the right and cuts inside onto his left. He comes across the face of the penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is off target.

Sabah are enjoying a decent spell of possession but have not yet threatened Lammens’ goal in this second half.

Is Yoro lucky? Mickels appeared to turn him not far outside the Manchester United penalty area but Yoro is not penalised. It did on first viewing look like a foul and would have been at least a yellow card.

We are back under way at Old Trafford. How quickly might Michael Carrick make changes with Sunday’s Manchester derby in mind? Well, he has made one change at the break as Mount replaces Tielemans. It is Mount’s first appearance of the season. Sabah have brought on Mbina at the break.

Those two goals late in the half completely change the complexion of the game and Michael Carrick’s half-time team talk. Good first 45 minutes back in the Champions League for United.

The first half is brought to an end and Manchester United are cruising towards victory on their return to the Champions League. It has all gone wrong for Sabah.

That is game, set and match before half-time at Old Trafford as the dam has burst for Sabah. Sesko is played in behind by Mbeumo and is one-on-one with Pokatilov. Sesko takes it around Pokatilov before putting it into the empty net.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Michael Carrick’s side have their second of the night not long before half-time and it is a well-taken goal. Cunha, from the left side of the box, plays it inside to Tielemans. The Belgian takes one touch before, on the turn, playing it back into the path of Fernandes, who finds the net with a first-time finish.

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

Fernandes has an effort from the edge of the Sabah box but blazes his effort high over the bar.

That’s a warning there for United. Fernandes gives the ball away in the middle with a heavy touch and Sabah break through the tall, languid figure of Lepinjica. Parris’ cross loops the far post where Mickels should have done better than steer an inviting header into the side netting. Bit of a let off for Carrick’s side.

Sabah should be level as they miss a sitter. Parris, from the right side of the box, clips a cross to the back post that picks out Mickels. He should score but puts his header into the side netting. That should have been the equaliser for Sabah.

Dorgu clips in a cross from the left side of the box and picks out Sesko, whose hooked first-time effort goes just wide.

Half an hour in and United have been in command. It’s not scintillating but they warrant their lead and punished a misplaced pass by Parris brutally. Mainoo is orchestrating the game in the middle of the pitch. Best player on the park so far.

Parris’ shot from the edge of the box takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner. It is wasted though by Sabah as the inswinger is easily caught by Lammens.

Tielemans steps in with a crucial interception inside his own box to deny Mickels the chance of a shot on goal.

The Brazilian has his first Champions League goal but it is gifted by Sabah. The visitors are threatening a counter-attack but Parris inexplicably gives the ball away on halfway with a dreadful pass across the pitch. The ball is then moved out to the left, where Dorgu crosses. He picks out Cunha, whose first-time effort with his side foot hits the Sabah keeper Pokatilov and goes into the net. A sense of frustration had been growing inside Old Trafford but Sabah have rather gifted Manchester United the opener there.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

Sabah give it away inside their own half and Manchester United flood forward towards the Sabah penalty area. Mbuemo drives forward and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before getting his shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at Pokatilov.

That is outstanding defensive work from Dasdamirov. Mainoo plays a quite sensational first-time ball in behind into the right channel to pick out the run of Fernandez. The Manchester United captain has Sesko waiting in the middle for the cross but Dasdamirov steps in with an absolutely essential interception or else Sesko would have had a tap-in.

Sabah need to be careful as now a few times they have been caught in possession deep in their own territory.

Cunha sends in a corner from the left that threatens to go in at the far corner but Sabah keeper Pokatilov catches it near his own line.

Sabah are making their Champions League debut and so too tonight are Cesc Fabregas’ Como, who have just taken the lead at home against RB Leipzig. Manchester United will travel to Como in late October on matchday three. Manchester United play RB Leipzig at home on matchday six.

Sabah have to negotiate a couple of Manchester United corners in quick succession and they do so. The visitors’ starting XI tonight has a very international feel to it:

Sabah FC have named a starting XI featuring 11 different nationalities 🌍🇰🇿 Stas Pokatilov🇩🇿 Akim Zedadka🇦🇿 Rahman Dashdamirov🇿🇦 Aden McCarthy🇵🇱 Tymoteusz Puchacz🇺🇿 Umarali Rakhmonaliev🇭🇷 Ivan Lepinjica🇯🇲 Kaheem Parris🇷🇸 Veljko Simic🇳🇬 Christian Nwachukwu🇷🇼 Joy-Lance… pic.twitter.com/ih5Sf1aeie

Mazraoui, despite starting at right-back, has already had three shots in the game. Two have been outside the box that have been blocked and the latest hits the side netting from the right side of the penalty area.

Mazraoui plays a pass forward into Cunha on the right side of the box and the Brazilian tries to beat Pokatilov at the near post but the Sabah keeper makes the save and pushes it around the post for a corner.

Sabah are able to clear their lines from Mbeumo’s delivery.

Sabah seem content to take risks on the ball deep inside their own half and play out from the back. Will that be a masterstroke or is it asking for trouble?

Sabah make their first foray into the Manchester United penalty area and there are appeals for handball. It did hit Dorgu’s hand but it was right down by his side and that is not a deliberate handball. Sabah do win a corner, which Dorgu heads away.

Sesko, fresh off what he thought was going to be the winner at Everton on Sunday, has been given the nod to start up top for the home side tonight. He is very close to closing the Sabah goalkeeper Pokatilov down inside his own six-yard box and that was nearly a horrific moment for the Champions League debutants a matter of minutes into their debut in this competition.

Sabah started their journey through the qualifying rounds of this comeptition back in the early parts of July so they have already played quite a number of games so far this season, in comparison to Manchester United’s three competitive fixtures coming into tonight.

As has been the case at every Champions League game this week, there is a moment silence to remember the victims of the recent deadly floods in Nepal.

We are under way at Old Trafford. Manchester United, three-time winners of this trophy, return to the Champions League whilst Sabah make their debut in the competition.

It’s 1,003 days since the Champions League anthem has been heard at Old Trafford and, to be honest, it feels longer. There are about 500 Sabah fans here tonight.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Old Trafford and we are moments away from kick-off. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Tonight: Sabah (home)October 13: Atletico Madrid (away)October 21: Como (away)November 3: Roma (home)November 25: Sporting (away)December 8: RB Leipzig (home)January 20: Bayern Munich (home)January 27: Villarreal (away)

Michael Carrick has made four changes for Sabah to the team that drew 2-2 against Everton. Benjamin Sesko is given his first start of the season with Marcus Rashford dropping to the bench. Luke Shaw was given an additional rest day on Wednesday and is left out of the squad. It makes sense with Sunday’s derby against Manchester City to come but it’s an early glimpse of the delicate balance Carrick will have to strike with his only recognised senior left back this season. Shaw can’t be expected to play every few days given his history of injury problems.

It looks like Patrick Dorgu will be operating at left back against Sabah. This is United’s 300th fixture in the European Cup, including qualifiers. On the subject of qualifiers, Sabah became only the sixth side to navigate four qualifying rounds to reach the European Cup proper, with their campaign starting back on July 7. That was the same day Argentina beat Egypt in the last 16 of the World Cup. The Azerbaijan club were only formed nine years ago so have had quite the ascent since.

At 8pm on Thursday night, Manchester United will kick a ball in the Champions League for the first time in three seasons.

It must mark the start of a permanent return to Europe’s premier club competition. If United are serious about once again challenging for the Premier League title and building a £2bn stadium, that must be the way forward.

This is only the seventh time in 13 campaigns that United have been in the Champions League and the implications have been significant.

As we speak, there have just been two goals scored in the last few moments in the two early kick-offs. Both home sides, Fenerbahce and PSV, have just equalised in their respective games.

Presenting your Champions League Reds 📋❤️‍🔥

Manchester United make their return to the Champions League as they host tournament debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan on matchday one at Old Trafford. It will be the first time that Manchester United have faced an Azerbaijani side in European competition.

Manchester United have one win, one loss and one draw to their name in their opening three Premier League games. They were seconds away from winning their second game of the season on Sunday but conceded a late equaliser at Everton. They last featured in the Champions League during the 2023/24 season, when they were eliminated in the group stage, and have won just one of their last nine games in the competition.

“It means an awful lot [to be back in the Champions League],” Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said. “Challenging yourself against the elite, the very best. This football club has been used to being the best. It is not something you can take for granted. We missed out on it for a number of years and now we are back. It is where we expect to be without getting ahead of ourselves. We have made huge steps to make it in, now it is about pushing into the next chapter and evolution if the squad and this is certainly where we want to be.

“I do not think it is a case of if we get to a certain stage it is a success and if we do not it is not. We have to embrace the new challenge that we are facing as a group and push to what we can push to. If we get further down the line in this competition then who knows? I am not writing anything off. But we are taking it step by step and we certainly are not getting ahead of ourselves. We have got a squad that is strong enough to compete.”

Sabah make their Champions League debut having been founded just eight years ago in September 2017. Back in April, they secured the Azerbaijan top-flight title for the first time in their history and also won the Azerbaijan Cup in May. They earned a spot in the Champions League group stages after beating Hapoel Be’er Sheva 6-4 on aggregate. In the previous three seasons, they have tried to reach the group stages of the Europa and Conference Leagues but failed to do so. They have won all three leagues thus far, including a 5-0 home win over Zira last Saturday.

Team news from Old Trafford to follow shortly.

#1436. Severe drought and warming increase the extinction risk of cacti

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Extreme climatic events are increasing in frequency and intensity with climate change1. Their effects on species’ distributions and extinction risk remain poorly understood2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9. Most species distribution models rely on long-term mean climate, overlooking potentially important nonlinear effects of extremes. Here we integrate new spatial data on severe drought10, including compounding effects of warmer temperatures, with a comprehensive curated dataset of cactus occurrences (648,316 records) and species distribution models to assess how severe drought alters projected suitable climatic area for 993 species of Cactaceae, a highly threatened family11 that is commonly considered drought tolerant. In 91% of cases, models including severe drought were better supported than mean-climate models. Across emissions scenarios (Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) SSP1-2.6 to SSP5-8.5) with 100-km dispersal, including severe drought increased the share of species losing suitable climatic area from 58–61% to 69–72%. The proportion of species projected to lose over a quarter of suitable area increased from 26–43% to 55–58%, and the proportion projected to lose over four-fifths increased from 1–15% to 25–35%. With severe drought, restricting dispersal from 100 to 0 km increased the share losing suitable area from 69–72% to 84–85% across SSPs. These declines reduced regional richness, with five bioregions potentially losing over 25% of species. These findings demonstrate that accounting for climatic extremes can alter assessments of biodiversity vulnerability under climate change. Integrating climatic extremes into ecological forecasting will be critical for assessing biodiversity loss and designing effective conservation strategies across taxa and ecosystems.

Given the data sharing agreement with iNaturalist and private contributors and the widespread risk of illegal collection in Cactaceae, occurrence data used for analyses are available only on request. Requests should be made through correspondence with the corresponding author and, depending on the taxonomic scope of the request, may require an agreement with one or more of the authors (data derived from BIEN or private contributors) or with iNaturalist directly, prohibiting further data sharing. Requests should include a complete list of data users and their affiliations, the purpose of the request, the taxonomic scope and a disclosure of any competing interests. Partially obscured iNaturalist data are available72. Average climatic data were retrieved from the CHELSA repository, version 2.1 (https://chelsa-climate.org/). SPEI drought data are available from the NASA Socioeconomic Data and Applications Center (SEDAC; https://www.ciesin.columbia.edu/data/globaldrought/). Soil layers were downloaded from the SoilGrids repository, version 2.0 (https://www.isric.org/explore/soilgrids). Expert distribution maps used to create Extended Data Fig. 7 were obtained from the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species and the IUCN SSC Cactus and Succulent Plants Specialist Group. Bioregion data were downloaded from a previous study52. All Figures and Extended Data Figures are directly reproducible from the Supplementary Information and code at Zenodo123.

All code is available at GitHub (https://github.com/mdpillet/DroughtForecasts) and archived at Zenodo123.
